original_test_intent: Verify the approved IOMMU-enabled configuration is actually active and amdgpu loads and binds all expected GPUs without IOMMU, DMA, driver, PCIe or XGMI errors.
original_method: Establish the approved BIOS/kernel IOMMU mode through the user-owned change path, reboot only under plan, then correlate cmdline, IOMMU/DMAR state, per-BDF driver binding, GPU visibility and complete logs.
manual_activity: Operator applies/supervises the approved firmware or cmdline change and reboot; engineer resolves the duplicate code and any IOMMU, binding or log anomaly and decides the DUT verdict.
required_inputs: Approved BIOS/kernel IOMMU-enabled setting and expected cmdline
Supported amdgpu/ROCm, kernel and firmware versions
Expected eight-GPU BDF inventory and binding topology
Maintenance, workload drain, reboot and rollback contract
Independent OOB access and protected evidence storage
safety_requirements: Capture known-good firmware/cmdline/GPU pre-state and verify rollback
Do not change firmware or boot parameters without explicit approval
Verify boot recovery and active mode before evaluating the driver
Stop on wrong mode, IOMMU/DMAR fault, missing/unbound GPU, boot, PCIe/XGMI, thermal or power error
Preserve complete evidence; do not force repeated reboot or clear logs
agent_execution_scope: Read and compare cmdline, IOMMU/DMAR groups/status and per-BDF binding after approved change
Collect amdgpu module/version, AMD-SMI inventory and full relevant OS/BMC logs
Report exact mismatch or fault without hiding lines through head/grep truncation
Do not set BIOS/cmdline, restart over workloads or issue DUT PASS/FAIL
engineer_actions: Assign a unique code or approve the distinct row142/row406 variants
Approve IOMMU mode, change/reboot/rollback and expected GPU topology
Resolve mode, boot, DMA or driver discrepancies and decide PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The first 40 grep hits are supporting evidence only; they cannot prove BIOS/cmdline policy, active translation mode, complete DMAR/IOMMU state or every GPU's driver binding.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: After the approved configuration/reboot, capture `/proc/cmdline`, authoritative IOMMU/DMAR state/groups, `lsmod`/module version, per-BDF driver links, AMD-SMI inventory and untruncated platform logs.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The enabled-mode condition, driver-load acceptance and source 10/20 timing remain explicit.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use a pre/post configuration ledger that proves the intended IOMMU mode at firmware, cmdline and runtime layers and joins it to every expected GPU binding and error domain.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds authoritative state and recovery proof without changing the enabled-mode test intent.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: No bandwidth stress or row406 evidence substitutes for mode and binding health.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Parameter spelling alone may not establish effective translation; platform-specific runtime evidence is required.

project_override_considerations: Project authority must resolve row142 versus row406 duplicate identity and define the supported enablement semantics; it may not merge IOMMU-driver and A2A-stress coverage or accept a truncated log as the oracle.
expected_evidence: Pre/post BIOS/OOB state and complete kernel cmdline
IOMMU/DMAR enablement, groups/domains and fault status
Kernel/amdgpu/ROCm versions plus eight expected BDF bindings and AMD-SMI visibility

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The same code labels an IOMMU-enabled driver-load test at row142 and an XGMI A2A bandwidth stress at row406. Their intents and evidence are materially different, so both stable variants are preserved pending authoritative identity correction.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Supported mode and recovery inputs can be supplied; static review is complete and no hardware outcome is inferred from their current absence.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve duplicate code Wistron-AMD GPU-00126-V002 between Compatibility row142 variant 6607ec9307e9e775 (driver loaded with IOMMU enabled) and row406 variant b1e2d1efd6251506 (XGMI A2A bandwidth stress): assign unique identities or approve distinct variants; for row142 define the authoritative enabled BIOS/kernel mode, expected cmdline/runtime IOMMU evidence, eight-GPU BDF map and approved reboot/rollback/OOB contract.

review_improvement: Replaces an unsafe truncated grep with layered proof of active IOMMU enablement, full per-GPU amdgpu binding and guarded reboot/recovery evidence.
independent_technical_reasoning: An IOMMU token can be present while translation is bypassed or devices use unexpected domains, and a globally loaded amdgpu module does not prove every GPU bound successfully. The oracle must align firmware policy, boot parameters, runtime IOMMU state and stable per-BDF binding after the same reboot; XGMI throughput from the duplicate-code row answers a different question.
